content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Supplier Concentration Fragility", "construction": "Using segment and 10-K text data (Compustat segments plus disclosed major-customer concentration under SFAS 131), compute the fraction of a firm's cost of goods sold attributable to its top identified suppliers, proxied by inventory/COGS volatility combined with a Herfindahl index of reported input categories. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Firms dependent on a concentrated set of suppliers face under-priced disruption risk; investors underweight the tail risk of input-side shocks, so these firms must offer a return premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high supplier concentration"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Momentum", "construction": "For firms reporting order backlog (Compustat item OB), compute the year-over-year growth in backlog scaled by lagged total assets, then take the change in that growth rate over the trailing four quarters. Form deciles at each fiscal quarter-end.", "rationale": "Accelerating backlog signals future revenue not yet in reported earnings; the market underreacts to this forward-looking non-price demand signal.", "higher_returns_for": "high backlog acceleration"}, {"name": "Working Capital Efficiency Surprise", "construction": "Compute the cash conversion cycle (days inventory + days receivable - days payable) each quarter. Define the surprise as the current CCC minus the trailing 8-quarter average CCC, standardized by its own historical standard deviation. Sort into deciles.", "rationale": "Unexpected improvements in operating working capital efficiency reveal management quality and future free-cash-flow gains that the market prices slowly.", "higher_returns_for": "low (most negative) CCC surprise"}, {"name": "Intangible Investment Intensity Gap", "construction": "Estimate a firm's knowledge-and-organization capital by capitalizing 30% of SG&A and 100% of R&D with perpetual-inventory depreciation, then compute the ratio of this intangible capital to book value of physical assets (PPE). Compare each firm to its industry median and rank the gap.", "rationale": "Accounting understates intangible-heavy firms' true asset base, causing systematic mispricing that resolves as intangibles convert to earnings.", "higher_returns_for": "high intangible-to-physical gap"}, {"name": "Dividend Smoothness Ratio", "construction": "Over the trailing 20 quarters, regress quarterly dividends per share on quarterly earnings per share; the smoothness measure is one minus the ratio of dividend volatility to earnings volatility. Rank firms cross-sectionally each quarter.", "rationale": "Firms that deliberately smooth dividends signal confidence in persistent cash flows; the market underappreciates the information content of dividend-policy stability.", "higher_returns_for": "high dividend smoothness"}, {"name": "Analyst Coverage Attrition", "construction": "Using I/B/E/S, count the number of analysts issuing estimates each month and compute the trailing 12-month net decline in coverage scaled by prior coverage. Sort firms losing the most coverage into a short-leg and stable/rising coverage into a long-leg.", "rationale": "Declining analyst attention increases information asymmetry and neglect; among neglected stocks with intact fundamentals, a return premium accrues to compensate for reduced visibility.", "higher_returns_for": "high coverage attrition among fundamentally stable firms"}, {"name": "Capex Cyclicality Beta", "construction": "For each firm, estimate the sensitivity (beta) of annual capital-expenditure growth to aggregate industrial-production growth over a rolling 5-year window using annual Compustat capex. Rank firms by this cyclicality beta.", "rationale": "Firms whose investment strongly co-moves with the macro cycle bear higher systematic investment-timing risk that is not captured by market beta, demanding a premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high capex cyclicality beta"}, {"name": "Earnings Announcement Return Consistency", "construction": "Over the trailing eight earnings announcements, compute the fraction that generated positive 3-day abnormal returns and the mean of those abnormal returns; combine into a consistency z-score. Rank cross-sectionally each quarter.", "rationale": "Persistent positive announcement reactions reflect a durable pattern of positive surprises that the market fails to fully extrapolate, creating an under-reaction premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high announcement-return consistency"}, {"name": "Debt Maturity Concentration", "construction": "From Compustat debt-maturity schedule items (debt due in years 1-5), compute a Herfindahl index of the maturity distribution; higher values indicate large debt maturing in a single near-term year. Rank firms each fiscal year.", "rationale": "Concentrated near-term refinancing needs expose firms to rollover and credit-market risk that is under-priced, so these firms carry a risk premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high debt maturity concentration"}, {"name": "Gross Margin Stability Premium", "construction": "Compute the coefficient of variation of quarterly gross margin (gross profit / sales) over the trailing 12 quarters. Sort firms into deciles by the inverse of this variability (stability).", "rationale": "Stable gross margins indicate pricing power and defensible economics that the market undervalues relative to headline growth, yielding superior risk-adjusted returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high gross margin stability"}]}
